payload.reason: The evidence provides a clear explanation of how variance is calculated in relation to model outputs, specifically through the Expected Gradient Length (EGL) method and its relationship to variance reduction.

claims.text: Variance is reduced by minimizing the expected variance over the test set, which is related to the Fisher Information Matrix.
Expected Gradient Length (EGL) measures the expected change in model parameters, which is linked to variance reduction in model outputs.
EGL computes the expectation of the gradient norm over all possible labelings to inform variance calculations.
